title: The Void Throne — weighted settlement simulation
method: Five fresh player agents plus one facilitator. Three starting foresight tokens; optional one vision per round. Weighted final party signatures. Trial A provisional rules retained. No digital tools required for the paper game. Nominal sixty-minute schedule, not timed human play.

findings.lead: Guild navigation and joint military authorisation passed with 8 of 11 leverage. The Guild and Ascendant signed; the Janissariat refused. All ships, crews and military assets survived. The Ascendant began with three foresight tokens, spent two and retained one.
sections: The trial made a concrete difference

Guild discretion passed provisionally, with both Guild players signing a temporary Wayfarer Council commitment. Military autonomy failed because the Guild security representative refused it; the Ascendant had agreed to test it. In round two, the Guild delivered Relief and maintained the route. Both army players subsequently moved from joint Navigation to accepting Guild discretion, expressly because that service occurred. The Guild gained evidence for its claim to authority, rather than simply paying for a temporary title.
Cooperation carried costs for all three parties

An aggressive first round was followed by a cooperative recovery round. The first Raid sustained the army but left Communities at 1. In the second round, Wayfarer service displaced one commercial voyage and delivered Relief; the ship returned intact and Guild leverage remained 4. The army voluntarily stood Spear down and offered Vigil, losing one Readiness. The same loss reduced the Ascendant’s army-backed leverage by one. The Ascendant also spent personal foresight and ultimately surrendered independent command. Communities recovered to 3, Beacon stayed at 2 and Readiness ended at 3. These costs purchased useful outcomes; this was not full cooperation throughout both rounds.
The third token preserves a powerful voice

The Ascendant spent Navigation foresight in both rounds, leaving one of three tokens. That remaining token is guaranteed by the two-purchase limit; this was not deliberate hoarding. Final weights were Guild 4, Janissariat 3 and Ascendant 4: 11 available, with 8 required. Only Guild plus Ascendant could pass as a two-party coalition. Both therefore held effective blocking power at this ending, despite there being no formal personal veto. With the same physical result and two starting tokens both spent, the weights would instead be 4/3/3, requiring 7: the factions could then pass without the Ascendant. This is an arithmetic comparison, not another played simulation.
Spending and peaceful decline changed the available coalitions

After the first round, Readiness 4 and two unspent tokens gave weights 4/4/6. Buying the second vision reduced the Ascendant to 5. The peaceful second round then reduced both military-linked weights, producing 4/3/4. Had the Ascendant declined that second vision, the same physical ending would give 4/3/5 and an 8-point threshold: Ascendant plus Janissariat could still pass. The actual Ascendant explicitly preferred information to retaining those coalition options.

The recorded approvals were Guild yes, Janissariat no, Ascendant yes. Eight supporting leverage met the threshold exactly. The same five decisions would fail under unanimous ratification. This demonstrates that weighting can produce a constitution despite continuing institutional dissent; it does not show that the dissenting army will cooperate afterwards. The army accepted Guild navigation but rejected joint military control because an outside veto could obstruct the combat needed to maintain conditioning. The Ascendant preferred joint command because ordinary Guard had helped recovery, while military autonomy’s Home duty would make that protection a breach. Future deadlock, compliance and recurring duties remain untested.
The foresight cost worked better than the foresight content

Both visions were bought before their contents or the current faction sheets were seen. Both were disclosed. The first warned about an unguarded Shared crossing; no Shared crossing was available or ordered. The second concerned Military passage and Repair plus private Trade; the actual Relief order triggered neither. No selected vision changed an operational consequence in this run. They informed precautions and confidence, and their purchase changed leverage, but this does not establish that the cards provide sufficiently useful foresight. Both Security visions remained unread. Grey Petrel was never spent.
What this run establishes—and its limits

Six distinct agents supplied the five player roles and facilitator; concurrency was limited, so independent conversations were scheduled in batches. Saved original submissions support the transcript and mechanical checks. One deliberately difficult personality mix was used. The Ascendant’s motivation and the rules both changed from the preceding trial, so the outcome cannot be attributed to voting weights alone. The final joint military article was not actually exercised provisionally: the observed Guard decision still used imperial authority, albeit with agreement from both delegates. These are evidence of willingness to cooperate and an actual successful navigation trial, not proof of a durable joint government or a timed human playtest.

GN.name: Venn
GN.temperament: Combative monopoly defender. Low willingness to compromise, high commercial risk tolerance. Treats compelled carriage as an attack on Guild independence. Will use a unilateral voyage to demonstrate leverage if credible.

GS.name: Sable
GS.temperament: Cautious contractual sceptic. Low-to-medium willingness to compromise, low personal risk tolerance. Distrusts oral assurances and military protection promises. Prefers an intact crew and explicit terms to prestige; can oppose their own teammate.

JN.name: Daro
JN.temperament: Transactional opportunist. Medium willingness to compromise, high aggression. Will offer a genuine deal but demands transport or constitutional autonomy in return. Comfortable with civilian costs if they purchase durable military power.

JS.name: Tarek
JS.temperament: Proud aggressive commander. Low willingness to compromise, high appetite for unilateral action. Hates standing down and treats Readiness loss as institutional decline. Not suicidal: can abandon an attack if shown it cannot meet an enemy.

A.name: The Sovereign
A.temperament: Demanding, pragmatic founder. Wants an empire that can govern without repeated personal intervention. High willingness to delegate when evidence supports it; cautious about unsupported promises. Will balance civilian recovery, a viable army, foresight costs and constitutional reliability. Retaining an imperial article is not a goal. May reject a package they sincerely judge unworkable, but cannot manufacture a personal-control requirement.

contributions.reason: NG protects the expertise and commercial discretion that fourteen years of petitioning have not secured. MJ gives the Guild an enforceable voice over violence that threatens our crews and customers.

Joint Navigation gives us a real say over passage and requires the freight vessel to be offered. Military autonomy prevents the crown or Guild from quietly standing down our conditioning. I will trade concessions for reliable transport or durable autonomy; neither a promise of consultation nor civilian goodwill alone preserves a capable force.

messages.text: The cohort has reached Readiness 4; the communities have fallen to 1. That result changes what service is defensible. My earlier military-lift possibility becomes a relief offer: one Wayfarer Council commitment attached to NG, with Relief intended and Lantern Maintain planned. We forgo our second commercial contract to carry food, not to accept perpetual compelled carriage. In return I propose MJ and a Vigil Council commitment attached to it, with Guard intended. This gives the army outside scrutiny, costs it one month of conditioning, and gives our crews protection. On the printed arithmetic it leaves Beacon 2, Communities 3 and Readiness 3. I claim nobody else has signed: these are concrete terms for their decision.

The Raid achieved conditioning, and the civilian loss I opposed also occurred. Readiness 4 gives us room to protect people next month. I support W1 as written: NG with Wayfarer Council attached, and separately MJ with Vigil Council attached. I am willing to sign our exact Wayfarer commitment to NG, sacrificing the second contract. That willingness does not depend on MJ passing. Lantern Maintain must remain our ordinary assignment; I will oppose diverting its crew into Shared. Under MJ I intend to approve Guard and refuse another speculative Raid. I understand these commitments lock availability, not the promised orders. Our own Navigation delegate controlling Relief, plus an actual Vigil commitment, gives this offer substance beyond an oral assurance.

messages.text: The Raid delivered the force we needed, but Communities 1 is too low to repeat that bargain. I support the substance of your relief offer and am willing to approve NG with the exact Wayfarer Council commitment attached: that approval can stand independently of Military. I do not accept MJ merely because we should rest for one month. My counter changes Military to MA, replaces the Vigil Council commitment with Vigil Home attached to MA, and changes the intended Security order to Restraint. Relief plus Maintain still produces Beacon 2, Communities 2 and Readiness 3 on printed effects. That restores a defensible civilian floor while securing military autonomy. I am willing to pledge Vigil Home on that exact MA article, subject to JS signing; I am not presently willing to pledge Vigil Council to MJ. One necessary pause should not become a permanent Guild veto over fighting.

contributions.reason: Successful combat has created room for one month without fighting. GN offers a real commercial sacrifice, sufficient to justify NG independently. MA with Home and Restraint meets our stated civilian and readiness floors while preserving the durable military power I value; MJ would surrender that power unnecessarily.

messages.text: The Raid preserved our force, but Communities 1 is a real cost and I accept responsibility for supporting it. Relief next month is now necessary. My counter changes Military to MA, the Janissariat commitment to Vigil Home attached to MA, and the Security plan to Restraint, with no Warrant.
